THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO OPEN-WATER TEST AND VALIDATE A NEW TYPE OF ELECTROMAGNETIC RESONANT POWER TAKE-OFF WAVE ENERGY CONVERTER COMPONENT TECHNOLOGY. THE ELECTROMAGNETIC RESONANT POWER TAKE-OFF CONSISTS OF A HIGH GEAR-RATIO MAGNETIC GEAR GENERATOR AND AN ADJUSTABLE MAGNETIC SPRING. THE PROJECT WILL COMPLETE OPEN-WATER COMPONENT TESTING AT PACWAVE-SOUTH AND VALIDATE THE PERFORMANCE CAPABILITIES OF THE ELECTROMAGNETIC RESONANT POWER TAKE-OFF TECHNOLOGY TO A TECHNICAL READINESS LEVEL OF 8. TO MITIGATE RISK, LABORATORY TESTING AND WATER-TANK TESTING AT OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED. THE TESTING AIMS TO SHOW THAT BY USING THE ELECTROMAGNETIC RESONANT POWER TAKE-OFF, WITH CONJUGATE CONTROL TECHNIQUES, THE WAVE ENERGY CONVERTER IS CAPABLE OF GENERATING POWER WITH A PEAK-TO-AVERAGE POWER RATIO OF ONLY 3:1.

THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ADVANCE THE SEARAY K2 AUTONOMOUS OFFSHORE POWER SYSTEM (AOPS) TO COMMERCIAL READINESS. AN AOPS IS A NEW CLASS OF WAVE ENERGY SYSTEM; IT IS A MULTI-PURPOSE PLATFORM THAT TARGETS BLUE ECONOMY APPLICATIONS OF PROVIDING POWER FOR REMOTE OFFSHORE AND SHORE-BASED MINI- AND MICRO-GRIDS. ONE TARGETED APPLICATION IS DELIVERING POWER AND DATA AT SEA (PDAS) FOR COMMERCIAL, DEFENSE, SECURITY, AND RESEARCH MARKETS THAT REQUIRE RESIDENT POWER AND DATA COMMUNICATIONS FOR THEIR OFFSHORE MOBILE AND STATIC ASSETS. WITHIN THIS APPLICATION, AN AOPS CAN BE THOUGHT OF AS THE COMBINATION OF AN OFFSHORE CHARGING STATION, DATA SERVER, AND CELL TOWER.

HYBRID HYDROPOWER-STORAGE UNITS FOR GREATER OPERATIONAL FLEXIBILITY

THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO INVESTIGATE THE AUGMENTATION OF STANDARD HYDROELECTRIC GENERATION UNITSWITH FAST-ACTING ENERGY STORAGE TO CREATE A HYBRID HYDROELECTRIC GENERATION UNIT, WHICH WILL BE CAPABLE OF FASTER RESPONSE, GREATER VOLTAGE AND REACTIVE POWER SUPPORT, AND GREATER FREQUENCY REGULATION FOR ACCOMMODATING LARGER PENETRATIONS OF RENEWABLES AND MODERN INVERTER-BASED LOADS ON THE GRID. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES THE CONSTRUCTION OF A 200 KW LAB-BASED HYBRID HYDROELECTRIC GENERATION UNIT THAT WILL SERVE AS A TESTBED FOR PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS AND MODEL VALIDATION. ONCE THE MODEL IS VALIDATED, IT WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO A HIGH-RESOLUTION REAL-TIME WIDE-AREA GRID MODEL TO INVESTIGATE THE BENEFITS AND ISSUES ARISING FROM LARGE-SCALE INTEGRATION OF HYBRID UNITS.

THE LAB-BASED TESTBED WILL BE USED TO INVESTIGATE SYSTEM PERFORMANCE, AND FOR MODEL VALIDATION. THE MODELS WILL THEN BE USED IN A TRANSIENT HIGH-RESOLUTION MODEL OF THE WESTERN INTERCONNECT UNDER SEVERAL TEST-CONDITIONS: THE SUDDEN LOSS OF LARGE-SCALE GENERATION TO TEST SYSTEM FREQUENCY RESPONSE AND RECOVERY, AND SCENARIOS WITH LARGE-SCALE PENETRATION OF WIND AND SOLAR, ESPECIALLY WITH LARGESCALE SOLAR ON PARTLY-CLOUDY DAYS, IN WHICH CONDITIONS CAUSE LARGE AND FAST FLUCTUATIONS IN POWER. A COMPREHENSIVE TECHNO-ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MARKET PLAN DEVELOPMENT WILL QUANTIFY COSTS AND BENEFITS, AND ILLUMINATE PATHS TO MARKET AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROJECT OUTCOMES.

LITTORAL POWER SYSTEMS, INC. (LPS) WILL DEVELOP AND DEMONSTRATE MACHINE-LEARNING-ENABLED SUPERVISORY CONTROLS ON A WAVE ENERGY CONVERTOR (WEC) DEVICE. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO DEMONSTRATE THAT, IN REAL-WORLD SEA STATES, THE USE OF MACHINE LEARNING (ML)-ENABLED SUPERVISORY CONTROLS CAN GREATLY INCREASE THE COST EFFICIENCY OF A WAVE ENERGY CONVERTER (WEC) AS COMPARED TO CONVENTIONAL PASSIVE CONTROLS. THE LPS NEURALWEC, A WIDE BEAM POINT ABSORBER (THE PREDECESSOR OF WHICH WAS A FINALIST IN THE DOE WAVE ENERGY PRIZE), WILL BE DEPLOYED AND TESTED IN THE OPEN OCEAN AT THE PACWAVE TEST FACILITY WITH AND WITHOUT THE PROPOSED SUPERVISORY CONTROLS. DEPLOYMENT AT PACWAVE FACILITATES DEMONSTRATION OF THESE IMPROVEMENTS IN (I) COMPLEX SEA STATES WHERE THE WAVE SHAPES AND INSTANTANEOUS FORCES ON THE DEVICE ARE NOT KNOWN BEFOREHAND, AND (II) LONG-PERIOD OPEN OCEAN WAVES, WHERE MOST CONVENTIONAL POINT ABSORBER WECS HAVE GREAT DIFFICULTY PRODUCING ENERGY EFFICIENTLY. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, LPS WILL ALSO MATURE THE NEURALWEC DESIGN ACCORDING TO INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS, DEVELOP DEPLOYMENT AND TEST PLANS, EVALUATE COMMERCIAL RISKS, AND PROVIDE DATA TO ADVANCE THE WAVE INDUSTRY TOWARD ACHIEVING COST COMPETITIVENESS IN BOTH NON-GRID AND UTILITY-SCALE MARKETS.

WITH THE SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN INTERMITTENT ENERGY RESOURCES SUCH AS WIND AND SOLAR, A POWER PLANT’S ABILITY TO PROVIDE FLEXIBLE OPERATIONS IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN EVER. THIS IMPORTANCE IS REFLECTED IN CURRENT REGIONAL TRANSMISSION ORGANIZATION (RTO) ECONOMICS AND UTILITY TARIFFS: UTILITIES CAN CREATE VALUE IN THEIR HYDROPOWER PLANTS FROM, AND INDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCERS CAN RECEIVE SIGNIFICANT PAYMENTS FOR, HAVING ON-DEMAND GENERATION AND ANCILLARY SERVICES SUCH AS FREQUENCY RESPONSE, SPINNING RESERVE, REACTIVE POWER AND BLACK-START CAPABILITY; WHICH ARE COLLECTIVELY REFERRED TO AS FLEXIBILITY SERVICES. HOWEVER, MOST UNITS IN THE INDUSTRY’S EXISTING FLEET OF TURBINE/GENERATORS ARE THE RESULT OF DESIGN DECISIONS MADE DECADES AGO WHEN THE ELECTRICITY SYSTEM LOOKED VERY DIFFERENT THAN TODAY. THIS GIVES RISE TO A MISMATCH, IN MANY CASES, BETWEEN A MACHINE’S OPTIMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS AND THE OPERATING RANGES REQUIRED FOR PROVIDING FLEXIBILITY SERVICES ON TODAY’S ELECTRICAL GRID, WHICH CAN HAVE A MAJOR IMPACT ON DAMAGE FROM WEAR AND TEAR. THIS IMPACT IS NOT A MINOR ISSUE: INCREASES IN DAMAGE FACTORS AS HIGH AS 400X HAVE BEEN REPORTED. IN RESPONSE TO THESE PROBLEMS AND OPPORTUNITIES, LPS CONCEIVED A RETROFIT OPERATIONAL FLEXIBILITY SYSTEM FOR LEGACY HYDRO PLANTS. THIS RETROFIT SYSTEM CONSISTS OF HARDWARE, ELECTRONICS, AND SOFTWARE COMPONENTS. THE SYSTEM IS INTENDED TO INCREASE A PLANT'S ABILITY TO CREATE VALUE BY GREATLY ENHANCING ITS ABILITY TO OPERATE FLEXIBLY WHILE DECREASING WEAR AND TEAR ON EQUIPMENT.

LAUNCH ALASKA PROPOSES TO DEPLOY A ROBUST AND UNIQUE TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM THAT COLLECTS AND ANALYSES DATA NECESSARY TO IDENTIFY VIABLE LOCAL AND REGIONAL ENERGY PROJECTS IN COLLABORATION WITH ALASKA COMMUNITIES, REGIONAL NATIVE CORPORATIONS, AND TECHNICAL ADVISORS. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP LONG-TERM STRATEGIES FOR DEVELOPING REGIONAL POWER PROJECTS UTILIZING LOCALLY AVAILABLE ENERGY SOURCES, GAIN BROAD CONSENSUS FOR PROJECT PRIORITIES AND DEVELOPMENT PLANS, ACCELERATE LARGE-SCALE DEVELOPMENT AND DEPLOYMENT OF RENEWABLE ENERGY, AND SUPPORT AN EQUITABLE TRANSITION TO A DECARBONIZED ELECTRICITY SYSTEM IN ALASKA’S UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES.

THIS PROJECT EXPECTS TO DEMONSTRATE THE POTENTIAL FOR UTILIZING A 3D VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT POPULATED WITH DATA FROM A VARIETY OF DIGITAL TOOLS, SUCH AS UTILITY GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS), ADVANCED METERING INFRASTRUCTURE (AMI) SYSTEMS, OR OTHER ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE, AS A MEANS OF IMPROVING STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND EDUCATION, STRATEGIC IDENTIFICATION OF PLACE-BASED ENERGY PROJECT OPPORTUNITIES, AND THE AGGREGATION OF PROJECTS SUFFICIENT TO FINANCIALLY PACKAGE THEM FOR DEVELOPMENT. THESE GENERALIZED LESSONS REGARDING ENERGYSHEDS WILL ENABLE THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY (DOE) TO REPLICATE THE OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT IN OTHER GEOGRAPHIES, COMMUNITIES, AND CULTURES, AND ENSURE TRADITIONAL AND INSTITUTIONAL KNOWLEDGE IS CAPTURED, MAINTAINED, AND INCORPORATED.

THE PROPOSED OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION FOR FUNDING IS TO DEPLOY USER-FRIENDLY TOOLS THAT ENABLE LONG-TERM STRATEGIES FOR DEVELOPING POWER PROJECTS UTILIZING LOCALLY AVAILABLE ENERGY SOURCES IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT WILL PRODUCE PUBLIC SUPPORT AND AN AGGREGATED FUNDING PACKAGE DEVELOPED FOR MORE THAN 3 LOCAL PLACE-BASED ENERGY GENERATION PROJECTS.

THE PROPOSED PROJECT SEEKS TO DEMONSTRATE INCREASED HYDROPOWER FLEXIBILITY BY HYBRIDIZING HYDROGEN 
ENERGY TECHNOLOGY WITH A HYDROPOWER FACILITY. THE PROJECT WOULD INVOLVE THE INSTALLATION AND OPERATION 
OF AN ELECTROLYZER, FUEL CELLS, AND INVERTERS AT A COLORADO SPRINGS UTILITIES HYDROPOWER POWER 
FACILITY IN COLORADO. ADDITIONAL WORK WOULD INVOLVE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT CONCERNING THE PROJECT AND 
DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION OF AN EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM RELEVANT TO TYPES OF ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES RELATED 
TO THE PROPOSAL. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WOULD INCLUDE SITE ANALYSES, ENGINEERING DESIGN, PERMITTING, SITE 
PREPARATION, INSTALLATION AND OPERATION OF EQUIPMENT, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, DATA ANALYSIS, AND 
DISSEMINATION OF FINDINGS.

ONE OF THE KEY OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A CONTROL SYSTEM THAT SEAMLESSLY INTEGRATES FLOATING SOLAR PANELS WITH THE EXISTING DAM HYDROPOWER INFRASTRUCTURE TO IMPROVE GENERATION RELIABILITY. COMBINING FLOATING SOLAR PANELS WITH HYDROPOWER ADDRESSES SEVERAL CHALLENGES, SUCH AS ENERGY INTERMITTENCY, VARYING WATER FLOWS, AND INFRASTRUCTURE CAPITAL COSTS. THE SUCCESS OF THIS PROJECT COULD LEAD TO THE INSTALLATION OF MORE FLOATING SOLAR PANELS ON HYDROPOWER RESERVOIRS, ENHANCING THE LOCAL WORKFORCE BY PROVIDING JOB OPPORTUNITIES IN SOLAR POWER GENERATION. IN ADDITION, INTEGRATING MULTIPLE RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES CAN OFFSET SEASONAL DROPS IN HYDROPOWER GENERATION AND MAXIMIZE GENERATION POTENTIAL ON HYDROPOWER RESERVOIRS.

GE VERNOVA ADVANCED RESEARCH (GEVAR, PRIME), GE VERNOVA’S HYDRO POWER (GEVH), PACIFIC NORTHWEST NATIONAL LAB (PNNL) AND UNITED STATES BUREAU OF RECLAMATION (USBR) PROPOSE TO DEVELOP DURABLE AND COST EFFECTIVE POLYMER BASED ADD-ONS TO INCREASE THE OPERATIONAL FLEXIBILITY OF THE FRANCIS RUNNER BASED HYDRO POWER FLEET (~45GW, 50% OF US FLEET). THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO INCREASE THE RAMPING CAPABILITIES AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE FRANCIS MACHINES, WHICH ARE KNOWN TO BE THE LEAST FLEXIBLE HYDRO UNITS.

negativeFlows.title: WITH THE SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN INTERMITTENT ENERGY RESOURCES SUCH AS WIND AND SOLAR, A POWER PLANT’S ABILITY TO PROVIDE FLEXIBLE OPERATIONS IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN EVER. THIS IMPORTANCE IS REFLECTED IN CURRENT REGIONAL TRANSMISSION ORGANIZATION (RTO) ECONOMICS AND UTILITY TARIFFS: UTILITIES CAN CREATE VALUE IN THEIR HYDROPOWER PLANTS FROM, AND INDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCERS CAN RECEIVE SIGNIFICANT PAYMENTS FOR, HAVING ON-DEMAND GENERATION AND ANCILLARY SERVICES SUCH AS FREQUENCY RESPONSE, SPINNING RESERVE, REACTIVE POWER AND BLACK-START CAPABILITY; WHICH ARE COLLECTIVELY REFERRED TO AS FLEXIBILITY SERVICES. HOWEVER, MOST UNITS IN THE INDUSTRY’S EXISTING FLEET OF TURBINE/GENERATORS ARE THE RESULT OF DESIGN DECISIONS MADE DECADES AGO WHEN THE ELECTRICITY SYSTEM LOOKED VERY DIFFERENT THAN TODAY. THIS GIVES RISE TO A MISMATCH, IN MANY CASES, BETWEEN A MACHINE’S OPTIMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS AND THE OPERATING RANGES REQUIRED FOR PROVIDING FLEXIBILITY SERVICES ON TODAY’S ELECTRICAL GRID, WHICH CAN HAVE A MAJOR IMPACT ON DAMAGE FROM WEAR AND TEAR. THIS IMPACT IS NOT A MINOR ISSUE: INCREASES IN DAMAGE FACTORS AS HIGH AS 400X HAVE BEEN REPORTED. IN RESPONSE TO THESE PROBLEMS AND OPPORTUNITIES, LPS CONCEIVED A RETROFIT OPERATIONAL FLEXIBILITY SYSTEM FOR LEGACY HYDRO PLANTS. THIS RETROFIT SYSTEM CONSISTS OF HARDWARE, ELECTRONICS, AND SOFTWARE COMPONENTS. THE SYSTEM IS INTENDED TO INCREASE A PLANT'S ABILITY TO CREATE VALUE BY GREATLY ENHANCING ITS ABILITY TO OPERATE FLEXIBLY WHILE DECREASING WEAR AND TEAR ON EQUIPMENT.
